thread.title: Stock Market Soars On IBM, Red Hat Merger; FANG Stocks Rally | Investor's Business Daily

author: KEN SHREVE
title: Stock Market Soars On IBM, Red Hat Merger; FANG Stocks Rally | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The stock market was in rally mode early Monday. Technology stocks rallied nicely after IBM ( IBM ) agreed to buy Linux software maker Red Hat ( RHT ) over the weekend for $33.4 billion, or 190 a share.
X The Nasdaq composite and S&P 500 led the way, up 1.3% each, in the stock market today. The Dow Jones industrial average picked up 0.8%.
The Nasdaq composite capped its fourth weekly loss in a row Friday, falling nearly 4% for the week. Over the past four weeks, it's down 10.9%. The market remains in a correction until proven otherwise, which means favoring cash is a good course of action for now.
European indexes ended broadly higher amid news that Germany's Angela Merkel would not seek a fifth term as chancellor after her term ends in 2021. Germany's DAX rose 2.1%; the London FTSE 100 added 2% and the Paris CAC-40 picked up 1.1%.
Stock Market Jumps At Open Blue chips rallied early in the stock market today, but IBM sat at the rally out. Shares dropped 4% on concerns Big Blue overpaid for Red Hat. Red Hat stock surged 48% in early trade to around 173. Shares closed Friday at 116.68.
There's no doubt the deal will make IBM a formidable player in the cloud market, an area dominated by cloud-computing giants Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Google parent Alphabet ( GOOGL ).

Please contact customer service CLOSE Dow stock Apple ( AAPL ) rose 1% ahead of its earnings report Thursday after the close. The strong-performing FAANG stock was featured as a possible call-option trade in the latest Earnings Preview column.
Dow components Visa ( V ), Caterpillar ( CAT ), Merck ( MRK ) and Nike ( NKE ) also outperformed in early trading with gains of more than 2%
FAANG Stocks On The Move Among other FAANG stocks, Facebook ( FB ) and Netflix ( NFLX ) outperformed with gains of around 2%. Meanwhile, longtime Leaderboard holding Amazon edged up 0.4% after slumping nearly 7% last week on earnings.
In other news, Brazil stocks looked to rally on news conservative Jair Bolsonaro won Brazil's presidential runoff election Sunday. Watchers see him as stock-market friendly, but the former army officer also praises the military dictatorship that controlled Brazil for several years.
The iShares MSCI Brazil ETF ( EWZ ) broke out over the 40 level. Shares were up nearly 3% in early trading.
After the close, watch for earnings from leading restaurant stock WingStop ( WING ). At a time when most growth stocks have given up major support levels, WingStop is still trading near its 50-day moving average. According to Zacks, analysts see adjusted quarterly profit jumping 12% to 19 cents a share, with sales up 47% to $38.19 billion.
